nodes.name: High-entropy MOF Synthesis
nodes.procedure: The synthesis of FeCoNiMoZn MOFs started with the dissolution of 0.25 mmol of Fe(CO₂CH₃)₂·4H₂O, 0.25 mmol of Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 0.25 mmol of Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 0.25 mmol of Zn(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 0.25 mmol of Na₂MoO₄, and 0.34 mmol of 2,5-dihydroxyterephthalic acid in the mixture of 22.5 ml of DMF, 1.35 ml of anhydrous ethanol, and 1.35 ml of DI water. Then, the mixture sonicated at least 60 min. Subsequently, the mixture was immediately transferred into a 50-ml autoclave and then heated to 120°C for 24 hours. The synthesized FeCoNiMoZn MOFs precursor was washed with ultrapure DI water, DMF, and EtOH in sequence for several times and dried for 12 hours at 70°C.

nodes.name: Spatial-Temporal Carbothermal Shock
nodes.procedure: A large current pulse (20 A, 100 ms) was used for CTS in an Ar atmosphere. The current output mode is adopted and the maximum output voltage is 30 V. The fast heating rate of ∼10⁴°C/s is achieved by an instant pulsing current to 10 A in 100 ms (∼100 A/s)

nodes.description: OER performance comparison of ST-HEA and control catalysts in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The electrocatalytic OER activity of ST-HEA and other control catalysts were tested in a three-electrode system in N₂-saturated 1.0 M KOH solution at room temperature (Fig. 3, J to L)... the MoZnFeCoNi catalyst exhibits the lowest overpotential of 221 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm⁻²... ultralow overpotential of 341 mV at a high current density of 500 mA cm⁻²... Tafel slope of the MoZnFeCoNi catalyst (48.78 mV dec⁻¹)... charge transfer resistance (R_ct) of ST-HEA is 2.5 ohm... C_dl value of the MoZnFeCoNi catalyst is 11.84 mF cm⁻²

nodes.characterization_summary: ST-HEA shows clear face-centered cubic (FCC) structure with diffraction peaks at (111), (200), and (220) planes, peak positions shifted compared to Fe-based and Ni-based alloys, confirming single-phase HEA formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the XRD patterns of ST-HEA illustrate a clear face-centered cubic (FCC) structure with distinct diffraction peaks attributed to (111), (200), and (220) planes.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS determines surface Zn content ratios of 5.75 at% in ST-HEA, 1.05 at% in T-HEA, and 0 at% in S-HEA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The content ratio of the Zn element in ST-HEA, T-HEA, and S-HEA are determined as 5.75, 1.05, and 0%, respectively (Fig. 2E and table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms bulk composition consistent with XPS results, showing highest Zn retention in ST-HEA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the bulk composition is also confirmed by the inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometer (ICP-OES).

nodes.characterization_summary: N₂ adsorption-desorption isotherms show BET surface areas of 139.25 m²/g for ST-HEA, 3.45 m²/g for T-HEA, and 81.61 m²/g for S-HEA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the surface area of the ST-HEA was analyzed by the BET (Brunauer, Emmett, and Teller), showing an exceptional BET surface area of 139.25 m²/g, higher than T-HEA (3.45 m²/g) and S-HEA (81.61 m²/g).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows ST-HEA as highly porous spheres self-assembled by nanoparticles connected by carbon framework.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the SEM result in Fig. 3D showed the shape of a highly porous sphere self-assembled by numerous nanoparticles connected by the carbon framework.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows uniform nanoparticle morphology of ST-HEA with size 12.81 ± 0.19 nm interconnected by carbon framework.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ST-HEA displays a uniform nanoparticle morphology with a size of 12.81 ± 0.19 nm, interconnected by the carbon framework.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes of 0.205 nm corresponding to (111) crystal face of HEA, with thin carbon shell covering alloy particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the lattice fringes were identified as 0.205 nm, ascribed to the (111) crystal face of HEA.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping confirms homogeneous distribution of Fe, Co, Ni, Mo, Zn, C, and N elements in ST-HEA without segregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS mapping of ST-HEA demonstrates that the five elements are homogeneously dispersed without element segregation after pyrolysis at high temperatures.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows M-O vibrations at 473.0 and 552.4 cm⁻¹ in M-OOH and oxygen-containing intermediates at 808, 914, 980 cm⁻¹ during OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a pair of bands at 473.0 and 552.4 cm⁻¹ appeared on the as-prepared catalysts assigned to M-O vibrations in M-OOH... The other three peaks at 808, 914, and 980 cm⁻¹ are all characteristic peaks of oxygen-containing intermediates.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS after OER shows O 1s peaks at 530.2 eV (M-O, 23.58 at%), 531.7 eV (M-OH), 532.8 eV (M-OOH), confirming surface reconstruction to MOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 4G shows the three oxygen peaks at 530.2, 531.7, and 532.8 eV that represent lattice oxygen (M-O), defective oxygen (M-OH), and adsorbed oxygen species (M-OOH), respectively.
